chunk: Travel & Expense Policy (EN, 202501) # Travel & Expense Policy Version: 202501 Company: Global Service Firm Region: Global (EN)

The Travel & Expense Policy outlines the guidelines for business travel and related expenses incurred by employees of Global Service Firm. This policy aims to ensure that travel is conducted in a costeffective, fair, and compliant manner while promoting sustainability. It applies to all employees traveling for business purposes, regardless of location.

1. CostEffectiveness Employees are expected to make travel arrangements that are economical and provide value to the company. 2. Fairness All employees should be treated equitably regarding travel and expense reimbursements. 3. Compliance Employees must adhere to all local, regional, and international laws and regulations related to travel. 4. Sustainability The company encourages ecofriendly travel choices and limits shorthaul flights when alternative options are available.

Employees Responsible for understanding and adhering to this policy, obtaining necessary approvals, and submitting accurate expense reports. Managers Responsible for preapproving travel requests, ensuring compliance with the policy, and reviewing expense reports for accuracy. Finance/HR Responsible for processing reimbursements, maintaining records, and providing support for policyrelated inquiries. Travel Desk Responsible for assisting employees with travel arrangements, preferred vendor bookings, and providing travelrelated information.

1. Booking System All travel arrangements must be made through the designated booking system. 2. Manager Approval Employees must obtain written approval from their direct manager before booking any travel. 3. Timelines Approval requests should be submitted at least two weeks prior to travel to allow for processing and adjustments.

Preferred Vendors Employees are encouraged to use preferred vendors for flights, hotels, and car rentals to ensure costeffectiveness. Flights Book flights at least 14 days in advance to secure the best rates. Economy class is the standard for all domestic flights. Hotels Employees should book accommodations within the company’s preferred hotel network unless otherwise approved. Car Rentals Use preferred rental agencies. Employees are encouraged to select compact or economy vehicles unless a larger vehicle is necessary for business purposes. Trains Train travel should be booked in advance and will generally be reimbursed at economy class rates.

Economy Class All employees are required to travel in economy class for domestic and international flights under 6 hours. Business Class Business class travel is permitted for international flights exceeding 6 hours or with prior managerial approval. Exceptions Exceptions to the class of travel must be justified and documented in the approval request.

Meals Employees will receive a daily meal allowance based on the location of travel. This allowance covers breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Per Diem A per diem rate will be provided based on the destination. Employees should consult the company’s per diem schedule for specific rates. Currency Handling Employees are responsible for converting foreign currency and should retain all currency conversion receipts for reimbursement.

section: Deadlines and Process for Submitting Expense Reports
chunk: 1. Submission Timeline Expense reports must be submitted within 30 days of travel completion. 2. Process Employees must complete the expense report form, attach all required documentation, and submit it through the expense reporting system.

Receipts Original receipts must be attached to the expense report. Digital copies are acceptable if originals are lost. Credit Card Statements Credit card statements may be submitted as supplementary documentation but are not sufficient alone.

1. Workflow Expense reports will be routed through the finance department for verification and approval. 2. Service Level Agreement (SLA) Expense reports will be processed within 10 business days of submission. 3. Approvals All expense reports require managerial approval before processing. 4. Audits The finance department reserves the right to conduct audits on submitted expense reports.

section: Remote Work Travel and Hybrid Work-Related Expenses
chunk: Employees working remotely or in a hybrid model may incur travel expenses for businessrelated meetings. These expenses must comply with the Travel & Expense Policy and require prior approval.

section: Travel Safety and Duty of Care
chunk: 1. Emergency Contacts Employees must provide emergency contact information to their managers before traveling. 2. Insurance The company provides travel insurance for all businessrelated travel. Employees should familiarize themselves with the coverage details. 3. Medical Employees should ensure they have access to medical care while traveling and carry necessary medications.

1. EcoFriendly Choices Employees are encouraged to choose ecofriendly transportation options, such as trains over flights for short distances. 2. Limits on Short Flights The company discourages flights under 3 hours where alternative transportation is available.
Failure to adhere to this policy may result in disciplinary action, including reimbursement denial or further consequences as deemed appropriate by management.

section: Example Scenario: International Trip Approval Workflow
chunk: 1. Employee submits a travel request through the booking system. 2. Manager reviews and approves the request, ensuring compliance with the policy. 3. Travel Desk books travel arrangements through preferred vendors. 4. Employee travels and retains all receipts. 5. Employee submits expense report within 30 days of return. 6. Finance reviews and processes the report for reimbursement.

section: Step-by-Step Guide for Filing an Expense Report
chunk: 1. Gather Receipts Collect all relevant receipts and documents. 2. Complete Expense Report Form Fill out the form accurately, categorizing expenses. 3. Attach Documentation Include all required receipts and supplementary documents. 4. Submit for Approval Submit the report through the expense reporting system. 5. Follow Up Check for approval status and address any queries.

1. What if I need to change my travel plans? Contact the travel desk immediately for assistance. 2. Can I travel with family members? Family travel expenses are not reimbursable. 3. What should I do if I lose a receipt? Submit a declaration form explaining the loss along with your expense report. 4. Are tips reimbursable? Tips for business meals are reimbursable within reasonable limits. 5. What happens if I exceed my budget? Any expenses exceeding the approved budget require prior approval. 6. Can I combine personal travel with business travel? Yes, but only the businessrelated portion will be reimbursed. 7. How do I handle currency exchange? Retain all currency conversion receipts for reimbursement. 8. What if I have questions about the policy? Contact the HR or finance department for clarification. 9. Are there limits on meal allowances? Yes, meal allowances are based on the destination and must adhere to company rates. 10. What if my travel is canceled? Notify your manager and the travel desk immediately, and follow the cancellation process in the booking system.  This Travel & Expense Policy is designed to provide clarity and guidance for all employees. Adhering to these guidelines ensures that travel is efficient, responsible, and aligned with Global Service Firm's values.
